question: What does the Latin phrase 'ex opere operato' mean in sacramental theology?

choices.A: Sacraments confer grace by the very act performed, not by the merit of the minister or recipient
choices.B: Only the sincerely faithful receive grace from a sacrament
choices.C: A sacrament is valid only when performed by a morally perfect priest
choices.D: Grace is given by work after the sacrament, through subsequent holy living

teaching.title: Ex Opere Operato
teaching.body: 'Ex opere operato' (Latin: 'by the work worked') means that a sacrament's efficacy comes from the rite itself as instituted by Christ — not from the holiness of the minister (ex opere operantis ministri) nor the prior faith of the recipient. This was defined against the Donatists (who denied sacraments given by sinful clergy) and reiterated at Trent against the Reformers. The recipient must not place an obstacle (obex), but grace is offered through the sacrament itself.
